Experiments show that ActECC reduces per-action latency by up to 27.4% and cloud calls by up to 45.1%, while lowering average execution error compared with existing edge-cloud collaborative.
item.dc:creator: Zihao Zheng, Zhihao Mao, Hui Huang, Sicheng Tian, Hangyu Cao, Ziyun Zhang, Chenyue Li, Jiayu Chen, Maoliang Li, Hailong Zou, Guojie Luo, Xiang Chen

item.title: A Density--Delay Law for Event-Driven State Progression in Open Distributed Systems
item.description: arXiv:2603.26758v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper studies delay-induced competition in an honest event-driven longest-chain network and distinguishes selected-tip divergence from lowest-common-ancestor (LCA) competing-branch depth. With density--delay load \(x_N=\lambda\Delta_{\max}\), regenerative analysis gives the explicit network-size-uniform bound \(\mu_N(x_N)\le e^{2x_N}+e^{x_N}-2\) on proposal-clock mean LCA depth. Bounded \(x_N\) suffices for this guarantee. At fixed delay, \(g(N)=O(1/N)\) is one corresponding input-rate scaling. An explicit finite-horizon depth-exceedance bound is also established. Explicit-node simulations show strong load effects and comparatively small finite-size effects. The results concern honest contention, not adversarial security.
item.dc:creator: Bin Chen, Dechuang Huang

item.title: Finding Nemo-Nemo: CFT DAG-based Consensus in the WAN
item.description: arXiv:2604.08914v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper introduces Nemo-Nemo, a practical crash-fault tolerant (CFT) consensus protocol designed to outperform existing protocols in wide-area networks by bridging design principles from the CFT and Byzantine-fault tolerant (BFT) worlds. By structuring command propagation through a causally ordered DAG, Nemo-Nemo allows all consensus replicas to propose commands with a naturally self-regulating communication regime. By exploiting multi-leader architecture, Nemo-Nemo avoids the performance bottleneck inherent to single-leader protocols. By separating command dissemination from consensus logic, Nemo-Nemo handles challenging network conditions even when consensus commits are stalled. Moreover, leader proposals that miss a deadline are never dropped, but deterministically deferred and executed later, preserving throughput under transient network delays. And by enabling Nemo-Nemo to commit on a DAG in just two network hops, it matches the latency of existing CFT systems, while achieving significantly higher throughput. The result is a robust, deployable system: the first DAG-based CFT consensus protocol proven to exceed state-of-the-art wide-area network performance in both speed and resilience.
item.dc:creator: Rithwik Kerur, Pasindu Tennage, Philipp Jovanovic, Dahlia Malkhi, Alberto Sonnino, Igor Zablotchi

item.title: KubePACS: Kubernetes Cluster Using Performant, Highly Available, and Cost Efficient Spot Instances
item.description: arXiv:2604.24027v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Cloud users aim to minimize cost while maximizing performance by selecting the most suitable instance types for their workloads. To reduce expenses, spot instances have been widely adopted due to their steep discounts compared to on-demand pricing. However, their use introduces reliability risks due to potential interruptions, and existing research has primarily focused on mitigating this trade-off from a cost or availability perspective alone. Despite the diversity in hardware capabilities among instance types, current provisioning systems tend to ignore performance variation, selecting nodes solely based on minimum resource requirements. In this paper, we present KubePACS, a Kubernetes-native spot instance provisioning system that constructs node pools optimized for both cost and performance while guaranteeing high availability. KubePACS formulates the node selection process as a multi-objective optimization problem, incorporating real-time data such as spot prices, performance benchmarks, and availability scores, including the multi-node Spot Placement Score (SPS). It solves this problem efficiently using an Integer Linear Programming (ILP) approach guided by the Golden Section Search (GSS) algorithm to find the optimal configuration. By integrating with the Karpenter node autoscaler, KubePACS jointly optimizes instance-type selection and node scaling decisions within a standard provisioning workflow. KubePACS also adopts a novel heuristic to support workload-specific preferences by scaling performance metrics for specialized instances. Through extensive evaluation across synthetic and real-world workloads, KubePACS demonstrates on average 55.09% and up to 81.06% higher performance per dollar over state-of-the-art solutions such as Karpenter, SpotVerse, and SpotKube, which only reference the spot instance prices and limited availability data.
item.dc:creator: Taeyoon Kim, Kyumin Kim, Enrique Molina-Gim\'enez, Pedro Garc\'ia-L\'opez, Kyungyong Lee

item.title: rush: Scalable Asynchronous Distributed Computing via Shared State in R
item.description: arXiv:2606.21430v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Many algorithms in statistics and machine learning can be parallelized in an asynchronous manner where workers need to communicate through shared state rather than execute independent tasks dispatched by a central controller. Especially in modern hyperparameter optimization and parallel black-box optimization with expensive objectives, this decentralized approach has become widespread, and several Python frameworks adopt it (e.g., Optuna, DeepHyper, and Hyperopt). However, all popular R packages for parallel computing follow a centralized controller-worker architecture that does not support this pattern. We present rush, an R package that provides a shared-state coordination layer for asynchronously parallelized iterative algorithms. rush uses a Redis database as a shared key-value store: workers read and write task data through the database and independently execute their own loops. The package provides a high-level API for managing tasks and their lifecycle, featuring sub-millisecond per-task overhead, robust error handling with automatic detection of lost workers, and efficient caching. rush optionally integrates with the mlr3 ecosystem, powering asynchronous optimization in the bbotk and mlr3tuning packages. We demonstrate the practical utility of rush by implementing asynchronous decentralized Bayesian optimization (ADBO) and benchmarking it on hyperparameter optimization of LightGBM across four datasets using 448 workers.
item.dc:creator: Marc Becker, Bernd Bischl

item.title: OasisKV: Scaling In-Decode KV Cache Beyond HBM with Lookahead Sparse Prefetching
item.description: arXiv:2608.08097v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large language model (LLM) inference serving is increasingly constrained by memory rather than compute. As long-context and long-form reasoning workloads become more prevalent, the key-value (KV) cache dominates both memory footprint and memory traffic at the token generation (i.e., decode) stage. HBM capacity has therefore become a critical bottleneck, constraining inference batch size and throughput. This paper introduces OasisKV, a memory-centric LLM inference system that alleviates HBM limitations by offloading the KV-cache to alternative memory tiers. Exploiting the sparsity of decode-time attention and leveraging speculative decoding to predict important tokens, OasisKV selectively prefetches and stages only the most relevant KV entries in HBM for efficient LLM inference computation. To support growing LLM context and the larger batches enabled by sparse HBM residency, OasisKV employs tiered KV management across decode, prefill, and remote-memory nodes, relaxing decode-host memory capacity limits under disaggregated serving. An asynchronous prefetch pipeline hides off-GPU transfer latency while bounding per-step traffic to fit the available bandwidth. We implement OasisKV on vLLM. With only 2,048 KV tokens resident in HBM, OasisKV maintains average accuracy within a negligible 0.61 points of full attention on LongBench v2 for long-context understanding and across AIME24-25 and GPQA-Diamond for long-form reasoning. This sparsity translates into a 1.86x throughput gain over vLLM on AIME24. Synthetic long-context workloads further show up to 2.2x higher throughput in multi-GPU serving. Under prefill-decode disaggregation, OasisKV achieves 2.29x vLLM's throughput while supporting 2.42x as many concurrent requests under the same host-memory budget.
item.dc:creator: Can Xiao, Sukmin Cho, Junbong We, Zhixiong Niu, Jianyi Cheng, Yiren Zhao, Youngjin Kwon, Yongqiang Xiong, Rui Ma, Junyi Liu

item.title: RT-HiSS: Ray Tracing Accelerated High Dimensional Vector Similarity Searches
item.description: arXiv:2609.01975v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recent GPU generations include special-purpose ray tracing (RT) cores for graphics applications. While RT cores are primarily used for rendering, recent works show they can be leveraged for general-purpose tasks, including similarity searches. However, existing approaches do not support datasets exceeding three dimensions. In this work, we propose RT-HiSS, the first exact GPU RT-core-based similarity search algorithm for high-dimensional datasets. GPU similarity search often scales poorly for large datasets with substantial search distances. To address this, RT-HiSS uses RT cores for fast index construction and searches, followed by candidate refinement on CUDA cores. We introduce a two-pass approach to estimate an upper bound on result size, enabling efficient batching under GPU memory constraints with near-perfect load balancing. Additionally, we examine shared memory tiling and compressed result masks to improve GPU resource utilization. RT-HiSS yields speedups up to 8.37$\times$ over competitive state-of-the-art GPU algorithms across six real-world datasets.
item.dc:creator: Revanth Reddy Munugala, Michael Gowanlock

item.title: Merge Hulls Without Copying Vertices: GPU Isotonic Regression
item.description: arXiv:2610.24038v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Isotonic regression finds the monotone sequence closest to the data in weighted least squares. It is used to calibrate probabilities and inside differentiable ranking. Its standard algorithm, pool adjacent violators, is sequential within a sequence, and torchsort, the exact GPU solver of differentiable sorting libraries, runs it with one thread per sequence, which is slow on long ones. The fit is the slope sequence of the lower convex hull of cumulative sums, and hulls of sorted points can be merged in parallel. Merging partial hulls level by level, however, copies the surviving vertices at every level, which moves Theta(n log n) data when most points survive. We store each chunk's hull once and represent a merged hull as a list of segments of these chunk hulls, at most one per chunk; a merge then updates the list. We prove the representation correct, bound the work and depth of the merge phase, and measure a CUDA implementation on four NVIDIA GPUs against a control that copies the surviving vertices with the whole GPU at every level. On dense hulls the merge phase is 17 to 276 times faster with segment lists and the whole operator 3.9 to 19 times; on noisy data, where few vertices survive, the difference is small. In a differentiable soft rank, replacing torchsort's isotonic solver makes forward and backward 1.8 to 820 times faster, and the training step of a compact model with a Spearman loss 1.5 to 40 times. Code: https://github.com/LenaBarretta/torchisotonic
item.dc:creator: Elena Raikova

item.title: FaaSpot: Fault-Tolerant Serverless Workflow Execution on Spot Instances
item.description: arXiv:2610.26709v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Serverless computing is increasingly used to run complex DAG workflows across diverse applications, and individual function execution times have grown to support them, pushing workflow makespans to hours. Open-source serverless platforms, deployed on a pool of VMs, typically use on-demand instances, and their cost increases with the makespan. Spot instances are far cheaper, but a preemption is likely before the workflow finishes. A preemption at a fan-out node or a task feeding a fan-in node stalls every parallel branch, cascading a single preemption into a workflow-wide failure. Prior systems address this challenge by migrating high-impact tasks to reliable, non-spot resources, sacrificing spot's cost advantage. We present FaaSpot, a serverless workflow execution system that runs every workflow task on spot instances with no on-demand fallback. Our key insight is that cascade-prone positions are determined by the DAG's topology and can be identified before execution. Therefore, FaaSpot analyzes the workflow DAG once at submission time and classifies each task by the impact of its preemption. Selective checkpointing, survival-aware scaling, and lineage-based retry then act on this single classification, with no runtime coordination. We evaluate FaaSpot on a trace-driven spot emulator with eight DAG workflows against four state-of-the-art baselines. FaaSpot completes 89.03% of runs at $0.018 per successful run, 21pp (percentage points) above the average baseline success rate and at a lower cost per success than every baseline, while reducing mean latency by 2.3x.
item.dc:creator: Bandhan Patel, Sushruth Harsha, Kwangsung Oh, In Kee Kim

item.title: Democratizing LLM Training with the Edge: Challenges, Systems, and the Road Ahead
item.description: arXiv:2610.32215v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The growing computational power of modern GPU data centers has let a few industrial giants train and deploy large language models (LLMs) on massive amounts of data. Yet the sheer scale of these models and their training data makes centralized development increasingly hard to sustain, and at the same time shuts out smaller institutions that hold relevant private data but lack comparable infrastructure. In this paper, we organize our positions on distributed LLM training around the pretraining and fine-tuning paradigms, covering federated learning, split learning, and decentralized approaches, and we assess their readiness for geo-distributed settings with heterogeneous hardware and unreliable connectivity. We then present a {\em unified} system architecture built around a cloud-hosted parameter server that coordinates heterogeneous clients over outbound gRPC connections, reusing one communication, compression, and fault-tolerance stack for both pretraining and a family of fine-tuning methods. We validate the design with real geo-distributed experiments on GPT-2 Medium and Llama3-1B pretraining across multiple university sites, showing stable convergence under realistic conditions. Finally, we chart the road ahead, identifying open problems that span frontier model support, elastic fault tolerance, adaptive compression, federated alignment, privacy and trust, incentive design, and system--algorithm co-design, all of which must be addressed to make democratized LLM training a reality.

item.title: Toward Open ISA Supercomputing: A Comparative Study of RISC-V, Arm, and x86 Architectures on HPC Workloads
item.description: arXiv:2610.32632v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: RISC-V is emerging as a candidate architecture for high-performance computing (HPC), but its competitiveness against established x86 and Arm processors remains difficult to assess because existing studies use different platforms, workloads, and methodologies, and rarely consider energy efficiency. Our work provides an evaluation of contemporary HPC RISC-V, Arm, and x86 processors using a common software stack and methodology. We characterize the Sophgo SG2044 and compare it with the NVIDIA Grace CPU Superchip and Intel Xeon Platinum 8480+ across four HPC benchmarks (STREAM, HPL, HPL-MxP, and HPCG) and four representative applications (iPIC3D, PLUTO, OpenFOAM, and llama$.$cpp). The version of HPL-MxP linked to OpenBLAS built and used for this work is made available as open-source software. The SG2044 reaches 8.02 GFLOP/s of FP64 performance and 7.8 GB/s of memory bandwidth per core, increasing to 294 GFLOP/s and 107 GB/s at 64 cores. L2-cache-aware process placement enables near-linear scaling up to 16 cores, beyond which memory-bandwidth saturation limits further gains. Across generations of RISC-V hardware, in the context of the Monte Cimone (MC) project, the SG2044-based MCv3 doubles both single-core performance and peak memory bandwidth relative to MCv2, while improving memory bandwidth, node-level FP64 performance, and energy efficiency by approximately 100x, 158x, and 10x, over MCv1. Against the Arm and x86 systems, the SG2044 shows 8-15x less absolute performance, reflecting its narrower vector resources and less advanced technology node, but delivers competitive scaling and energy efficiency on several workloads. Its most notable result is LLM decode, where 64-core execution provides the highest relative scaling and energy efficiency among the evaluated platforms while exceeding Intel in throughput. Our results show that RISC-V processors are closing the gap with the competition.
item.dc:creator: Emanuele Venieri, Giacomo Madella, Gabriele Ceccolini, Simone Manoni, Federico Ficarelli, Filippo Barbari, Jenny Lynn Almerol, Elisabetta Boella, Nitin Shukla, Simone Bn\`a, Luca Benini, Andrea bartolini

item.title: Multi-Agentic AI for Fairness-Aware and Accelerated Multi-modal Large Model Inference in Real-world Mobile Edge Networks
item.description: arXiv:2602.07215v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Generative AI (GenAI) has transformed applications in natural language processing and content creation, yet centralized inference remains hindered by high latency, limited customizability, and privacy concerns. Deploying large models (LMs) in mobile edge networks emerges as a promising solution. However, it also poses new challenges, including heterogeneous multi-modal LMs with diverse resource demands and inference speeds, varied prompt/output modalities that complicate orchestration, and resource-limited infrastructure ill-suited for concurrent LM execution. In response, we propose a Multi-Agentic AI framework for latency- and fairness-aware multi-modal LM inference in mobile edge networks. Our solution includes a long-term Global Planning Agent, a short-term Prompt Scheduling Agent, and multiple on-node LM Deployment Agents, all powered by foundation language models. These agents cooperatively optimize prompt routing and LM deployment through natural language reasoning over runtime telemetry and historical experience. To evaluate its performance, we further develop a city-wide testbed that supports network monitoring, containerized LM deployment, intra-server resource management, and inter-server communications. Experiments demonstrate that our solution reduces average end-to-end latency by 42.9% compared with a state-of-the-art online-learning baseline and by 80.6% compared with the full-activation baseline, while maintaining a mean service-type Jain's index of 0.925. Moreover, our solution adapts quickly without fine-tuning, offering a generalizable solution for optimizing GenAI services in edge environments.
item.dc:creator: Haiyuan Li, Hari Madhukumar, Shuangyi Yan, Yulei Wu, Dimitra Simeonidou

item.title: Certified Split Points for Parallel Lexing: Exact and Modulo Discarded Tokens
item.description: arXiv:2608.03473v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Table-driven DFA lexing is sequential, since each transition depends on the previous byte's state. Scanning one input in parallel needs each chunk's entry state, which existing methods recover by simulation, speculation, prescanning, or overlap. We give two conditions under which none is needed. For a longest-match scanner restarting from q0 at every token boundary, a byte b is a certified split symbol when no reachable state other than q0 has a b-transition whose target can reach acceptance, and q0 is not re-entrant if it has one. Every occurrence of such a byte in completely tokenizable input begins a token, so chunks starting there reproduce the serial sequence of kinds and lengths. The condition is necessary and sufficient, but one string, comment, or whitespace run can remove every useful certificate. Comments and whitespace are usually discarded, so we weaken the guarantee to equality after deleting a declared discarded set and give a second condition, a precomputed constant-time one-bit test. It is sound but incomplete and more permissive, strictly so on suitable token sets and discarded sets. It recovers newline for a conventional C-like tokenization and tab, newline and carriage return for JSON, and refuses newline where block comments are unrestricted. Safety modulo the discarded set is decidable in PSPACE for every token automaton and in polynomial time for literal vocabularies, and every unsafe byte has a replayable counterexample. On the fifteen token sets studied the second condition is already exact. Splitting at exact certificates in munch reaches 92.6-95.3% parallel efficiency at eight threads on a restricted CPU set and a 512 MiB corpus, and a 3.46-3.94x end-to-end speedup at four threads, on one machine. It turns delimiter-based parallel lexing from a language-specific assumption into a property a compiler checks.
item.dc:creator: Nicklas Nidh\"ogg

item.title: Truly Work-efficient Parallel Deterministic $(\Delta+1)$-coloring and Maximal Independent Set
item.description: arXiv:2608.08296v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give deterministic parallel algorithms that compute a $(\Delta+1)$-coloring and a maximal independent set for a simple graph with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges in $O(n+m)$ work and $O(\mathrm{poly}\log n)$ depth.
item.dc:creator: Chase Hutton, Adam Melrod

item.title: Dispatch Overhead, Not Kernel Quality: The Performance Bottleneck in Single-Stream WebGPU LLM Inference
item.description: arXiv:2608.08730v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Large Language Models are increasingly deployed in resource-constrained, single-stream settings, from internet browsers to edge devices, where requests arrive one at a time at batch size 1 rather than in large batches. In this regime, where WebGPU serves as a modern cross-platform standard, per-operation dispatch overhead, rather than kernel compute, can dominate inference cost, yet it remains poorly characterized. In this work, we introduce a sequential-dispatch measurement method and show that naive single-operation measurements overestimate per-dispatch cost by conflating dispatch with synchronization. Using our method, we measure the per-dispatch cost and show that it is independent of data type used. Through a controlled fusion experiment, we show that the dispatch overhead, not kernel quality, is the bottleneck at batch size 1, and isolate the dispatch count as the cause. We conclude that at batch size 1, the effective approach to LLM inference optimization in WebGPU is reducing dispatch count. Our findings point to dispatch amortization, in the inference engines and in the WebGPU specification, as a path to practical browser-based inference.
item.dc:creator: J\k{e}drzej Maczan

item.title: Certified Split Windows for Parallel Lexing: Recovering Boundaries Where No Byte Certifies
item.description: arXiv:2608.09761v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A certified split point lets a parallel lexer cut unlexed input at a single byte with the serial token stream provably preserved, but several conventional token sets in the predecessor's controlled study certify no byte once string, comment, or whitespace-run forms are included (arXiv:2608.03473v2). We generalize from a byte to a bounded window, a byte string after which the position where the current token began is known, regardless of surrounding context. We certify the directly usable form of that recovery, namely that the token covering the window's final byte begins at the reported origin. The certificate is conditional on occurrence and may be vacuous; every applicability figure counts only windows carrying an asserted completely tokenizable occurrence witness. We give a conservative model of a maximal-munch scanner's possible histories across a window, prove it sound, and decide reachability in that model exactly by exhausting a finite quotient of its reachable configurations. Within the flat, completely tokenizable scope, model-positive answers are semantic certificates; negatives are relative to the model, which deliberately refuses some windows a greedy scanner would allow. Whether the model certifies any window, plain or witnessed, is PSPACE-complete, and a shortest window can need $2^{\Omega(\sqrt{n})}$ bytes over n live states. Two smaller searches decide plain model existence, the second shipped in release 2.2.0 of munch. In a sample of 400 random token sets, 322 of the 337 sets certifying no byte gain a witnessed window, with zero inconclusive searches, and every exact-empty row of the predecessor's study gains a witnessed window of two to four bytes. The analysis runs once after automaton construction, using only the compiled tables and no input. A boundary profile marks each gap of a window forced, crossed or open, and a window-local cut is sound exactly at forced gaps.

item.title: A Cloud-Edge System for Multimodal Clinical Screening in Resource-Constrained Rural Settings
item.description: arXiv:2608.12745v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Medical AI has demonstrated specialist-level diagnostic accuracy, yet these capabilities remain largely inaccessible in resource-constrained rural settings where bandwidth is scarce, compute is limited, and clinical decision-making requires integrating heterogeneous modalities. We introduce a cloud--edge collaborative architecture that addresses these constraints: lightweight, domain-specific models on the edge transform raw medical data into compact structured outputs, while a cloud LLM synthesizes these outputs into clinical summaries. An LLM-based orchestrator dynamically selects diagnostic tools based on patient context, promoting comprehensive modality coverage without processing irrelevant inputs. We evaluate on 20 multimodal clinical cases spanning cardiac, obstetric, trauma, and screening scenarios under three simulated network profiles (500,kbps--5,Mbps). The hybrid system achieves 98--99% diagnostic tool recall with 92--96% precision, matches or exceeds cloud-only baselines on clinical accuracy, and maintains bandwidth-invariant latency (25--35,s) at 4--15x lower token cost. These results highlight the role of architectural design in enabling efficient multimodal integration and improving factual grounding compared to cloud-only approaches under deployment constraints.

item.title: HARTS: A Prefix-Sharing Training System for Agentic RL with Hybrid-Attention Models
item.description: arXiv:2608.28158v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Agentic reinforcement learning (RL) generates irregular rollout trees, but trajectory-by-trajectory training recomputes their shared interaction histories. Existing training-time prefix-reuse systems do not jointly address state recovery, dense execution, and distributed training for hybrid-attention models. We present HARTS (Hybrid-Attention RL over Tree Structures), to our knowledge the first system to demonstrate training acceleration from arbitrary rollout-tree prefix sharing on real hybrid-attention models. A two-level planner constructs compression-oriented microbatches, then jointly refines their membership, cross-microbatch sharing, placement, and execution order. Within each sharing window, gradients from dependent microbatches accumulate before one backward pass through the shared prefix computation. Differentiable boundary-state handoff and bounded replay preserve the per-trajectory chunkwise numerical path, while a linear-time planner attains the global minimum number of sequential linear-attention calls under our packed chunkwise-call model. The runtime uses a common compact layout across attention and dense or mixture-of-experts (MoE) layers, with support for distributed parallelism and activation recomputation. Recovering log-probabilities for each original trajectory position preserves RL objectives; for deterministic top-k routing without token dropping, occurrence counts restore MoE objective weights and expert-load statistics. On SWE-bench, HARTS delivers 4.77-10.45x the update throughput of trajectory-expanded training across two sampling schemes on 7.9B- and 124B-parameter hybrid-attention MoE models using 8-64 GPUs. On the 7.9B model, full-model logit differences are comparable to baseline self-rerun variation. The 124B model shows stable online learning trends through step 150 on SWE-bench and $\tau^3$-Bench.

item.title: MedCache: Efficient and Temporally Valid Memory for Longitudinal Clinical Agents
item.description: arXiv:2608.29528v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Longitudinal clinical agents must maintain an evolving patient state from evidence distributed across visits, time points, and specialties. However, how agent memory should be designed for this setting remains unclear. We introduce a benchmark of multi-visit, multi-specialty patient records that evaluates long-context evidence retrieval, cross-time evidence aggregation, and cross-specialty clinical reasoning. Using this benchmark, we systematically study four memory design choices: curation, organization, retrieval, and memory-augmented reasoning. We find that temporal validity is more important than simply retaining more history; specialty-factorized memory reduces context but can hide shared evidence; and multiple agents help when specialists must reason together, not merely when evidence comes from multiple memories. Guided by these findings, we propose \textit{MedCache}, a hybrid framework that constructs temporally valid patient memory, organizes evidence into overlapping specialty views, routes each query to relevant memories, and adaptively invokes one or multiple specialists. Experiments show that MedCache improves reasoning accuracy and memory efficiency over strong single-agent and multi-agent baselines, while generalizing across model backbones and external datasets.

item.title: Peer-Relative Trust-Guided Update Screening for Robust Semi-Decentralized Federated Learning under Label-Flipping Attacks
item.description: arXiv:2610.25714v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Trust and reputation mechanisms can reduce the influence of malicious clients in federated learning (FL), but strict update filtering is difficult under non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data because honest local updates may temporarily reduce performance on a shared validation proxy. Extending an earlier trust-based semi-decentralized FL (SDFL) framework, this paper operationalizes the trust signals and introduces peer-relative update screening that combines a robust validation-utility score with direction- and norm-based update quality. The method is evaluated with 50 MNIST clients, 20% persistent label-flip attackers, Dirichlet heterogeneity levels of 0.5 and 0.1, 100 communication rounds, and five paired random seeds. Under moderate heterogeneity, the proposed method reaches 98.37% final accuracy while rejecting 95.82% of malicious updates and retaining 90.30% of benign updates; the final benign and malicious trust distributions are completely separated (KS=1.00). Under severe heterogeneity, it reaches 95.25% accuracy, rejects 88.55% of malicious updates, and retains 76.90% of benign updates (KS=0.96). Trust weighting alone preserves slightly higher utility in the most heterogeneous condition, but accepts all malicious submissions. The results therefore distinguish influence mitigation from explicit containment and quantify the utility-selectivity trade-off introduced by screening. The study provides an empirically validated off-chain governance core that can feed blockchain-based audit and incentive layers in SDFL.

item.title: Amplified Pruning and Path Selectors for Deterministic Radio Gossiping
item.description: arXiv:2610.28930v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study deterministic gossiping in unknown strongly connected directed radio networks with $n$ vertices, $m$ arcs, and distinct identifiers in $[N]$, where $N=n^{\mathcal O(1)}$. Messages are unrestricted and collision detection is unavailable. Our neighborhood-clearing procedure reuses an elected receiver to secure its entire closed in-neighborhood in $\mathcal O(n\log^2n\log\log n)$ rounds. Charging each distinct closed neighborhood once yields $\mathcal O(m\log^2n\log\log n)$ rounds under an explicit degree-concentration condition, for every polynomial identifier range. A complementary adaptive-pruning procedure combines quadratic contraction with completion sensitive to the number of unsecured sources. If $a\ge1$ sources remain at completion entry, permutation selectors reduce the balanced completion budget by a factor of $\log^{2/3}(a+1)$ relative to interleaved path selectors. A geometric execution attains $\widetilde{\mathcal O}(k^2+n\tau+\min\{u^2,(nu)^{2/3}\})$ for a path cover of scale $k$, weight $\tau$, and $u$ exceptions. For directed graphs with common in- and out-degree $\Delta$, the portfolio achieves $\widetilde{\mathcal O}(\min\{n\sqrt\Delta,n^2/\Delta\})$. Every graph also admits $\widetilde{\mathcal O}(\min\{n^{4/3},N+(mn)^{3/5}\})$ rounds. Only $n,N$ are inputs; degrees, covers, and structural constants are used solely in the analysis. The unrestricted polynomial-identifier density extension remains open.

item.title: HyScale: Scaling Long-Context Training for Learned Sparse Attention
item.description: arXiv:2610.32057v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present HyScale, a long-context training system for learned sparse attention. Learned sparse attention is a promising architecture for million-token contexts, widely adopted in production since DeepSeek-V3.2. Selection, however, grows into the training bottleneck. For each query, it scores every previous token whereas sparse attention reads only $k$; worse, current systems materialize a full score table and repeat selection during recomputation. Our key insight is that the output of selection is not an activation, but rather a set of indices. Building on it, HyScale introduces HyTopK and selection replay. HyTopK finds each query's exact top-$k$ on the fly without a score table, while selection replay reuses forward-pass selection in recomputation. Together with holistic system optimizations tackling end-to-end training challenges, HyScale speeds up GLM-5.1 training on 1M-token sequences by 2.07$\times$ over Megatron-LM on 512 H20 GPUs. It also speeds up the CSA layers of DeepSeek-V4-Flash and the QSA layers of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next by 2.01$\times$ and 1.57$\times$ at 1M tokens on 32 H800 GPUs.
